maya: heads up — we're seeing a big retry spike and uneven fanout for svc ip 10.0.56.21 -> backend pool 'gpu-serving' in eu-west. One pod is taking ~70% of connections, others almost idle. Started ~2h after the node kernel roll (6.2.4). :thinking:
samir: any metrics or ipvs stats? is kube-proxy in ipvs mode or iptables?
maya: kube-proxy is ipvs. ipvsadm shows a single destination getting hammered.
maya: ipvs stats snapshot:
```
IP Virtual Server version 1.2.1 (size=4096)
Prot LocalAddress:Port Scheduler Flags
  -> RemoteAddress:Port           Forward Weight ActiveConn InActConn
TCP 10.0.56.21:80 rr
  -> 10.10.2.34:80                  Masq    1      12345      33
  -> 10.10.2.35:80                  Masq    1       234       2
  -> 10.10.2.36:80                  Masq    1        45       0
```
li: interesting — we did a perf test last night that toggled RDMA/MTU on a subset of nodes. Could be an MTU mismatch (9000 vs 1500) somewhere.
cory: also seeing conntrack entries pinned to one backend hash. When ipvs chooses dest by skb hashing, MTU/fragmentation can change paths or cause retries.
ops-bot: Incident-1234 created (P2) for service gpu-serving — https://redwood/incident/1234
samir: quick mitigation: we can pivot the affected nodepool to iptables (daemonset override) to force kube-proxy to use iptables mode on that pool. Not ideal long-term but will spread load.
li: can ipvs be tweaked to randomize selection more? ipvsadm has some options but not a silver bullet if conntrack/hash seeds changed.
maya: tried iptables on a single nodepool canary — distribution improved but median latency went up ~30ms. That confirms ipvs path is the trigger for the extreme skew.
cory: next debug steps: tcpdump svc VIP + backend nic, collect `conntrack -L` and `ipvsadm -Ln --stats`, and check kernel dmesg for ipvs/nf_conntrack warnings.
maya: attaching brief log snippet from ingress controller showing retries and 502s:
```
2026-03-17T10:12:03Z ingress: upstream_reset connection_reset by peer to 10.10.2.34:80 after 2 attempts
2026-03-17T10:12:03Z router: retrying request to backend, attempt=3
2026-03-17T10:12:04Z proxy: 502 from upstream 10.10.2.34, connection aborted
```
samir: I dug into the kernel roll — seems 6.2.4 changed the conntrack hashseed/probing behavior on some NIC/driver combos. If conntrack hash or skb hashing algo changes during a rolling update, existing ipvs mappings can become invalid or biased.
li: that would explain why skew appeared cluster-wide but only in eu-west nodepool that received the roll. Also check `ip link`/`bridge` MTU on that nodepool vs control-plane. We saw one node where the OVS bridge MTU was 1500 while NIC was 9000.
maya: agreed. action plan I'm proposing:
- rollback kernel on one canary node group (blue) immediately (oncall)
- run MTU audit across nodepools, ensure bridge and nic MTU alignment
- collect tcpdumps from VIP and backend NICs for 30m window
- add ipvs stats collector to console dashboards to detect skew automatically
- open bug with kernel vendor if confirmed

cory: I'll open a PR to add an MTU check in our node health probe and a small alert: "bridge MTU != nic MTU". Also will add ipvs skew grafana panel.
oncall: rolling back 3 nodes in the eu-west gpu pool now. ETA ~20m. Will post progress. :hammer_and_wrench:
maya: thanks. once rollback stabilizes, we'll re-run a canary traffic test and verify even distribution. I'll update Incident-1234 with results.
samir: long-term we should consider avoiding ipvs on nodes with mixed MTU/RDMA config until we standardize. Also schedule kernel-compat CI before mass rollouts.
li: noted — adding a preflight to the RDMA/MTU rollout playbook.
maya: for now, everyone monitor: errors, ipvs stats, conntrack table saturation, and backend pod CPU (maybe the hot pod is overloaded). Ping if you see >10% retry rate on that svc. :eyes:
cory: acknowledged.
oncall: rollback done on 3 nodes; traffic is rebalancing on canary. will continue rolling until all eu-west nodes are at the previous kernel.
maya: great — thanks team. I'll keep incident open until we have MTU audit + dashboard panels merged. :thumbsup:
